newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - March 24.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - March 24.

text.p: HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - Despite initial negative forecasts, GDP grew by 4.4%, and reached 1,186.6 billion crowns in real terms. The unexpected growth should be attributed to the final quarter of the year where a 4.7% increase was recorded.

- Ceska Pojistovna expects to record a loss of 5.3 billion crowns based on preliminary reports prior to auditing. The insurance company maintains that it would have recorded a profit of 2.7 billion crowns if it did not have to factor in high risk losses such as Kreditni banka and Kabel Plus.

- Stagnation or a minor drop in the price of meat and meat by-products have helped characterise the food product market since the begining of the year. Although prices of certain choice cuts of beef and pork rose marginally, the overall trend indicated a minor decrease.

MLADA FRONTA DNES - The Civic Democratic Party (ODA) elected former Czech ambassador to the U.S., Michael Zantovsky as its new leader. The former diplomat promises to change the style of the party by proceeding more diplomatically when negotiating with other heads of the coalition.

- Premier Vaclav Klaus said that no measures will be implemented to freeze wage increases. Klaus said that despite the fact that wages are increasing far too rapidly in the Czech Republic, the introduction of measures to curtail this trend would be incorrect.

LIDOVE NOVINY - Senate chairman Petr Pithart stated that Czech citizens are inadequately informed about preparations to join NATO. According to Pithart, the debate on NATO membership has only been conducted within the governing coalition.

- Financially troubled aircraft manufacturer Aero Vodochody has signed an agreement with Taiwan's Aerospace Industrial Development Corporation (AIDC) to form a joint venture to develop a new light commuter aircraft.

PRAVO - The Czech government will implement aspects of Vladimir Dlouhy's status report on Poldi Kladno, after initially rejecting it last week for being too unspecific. Parts of the programme which are to enable small and medium businesses to offer employment opportunities in Kladno have been passed and are being put into effect.
